EnCommReasonFlags.description: Flags: names of the set bits joined by ", " ("Client, Expert"), "None" when none is set; a set bit without a name is "Bit<n>" (bit number). Bits: Client = 0x1, Expert = 0x2, Dealer = 0x4, ExternalClient = 0x8, Mobile = 0x10, Web = 0x20, Signal = 0x40. Accepted on input, never written: All = Client, Expert, Dealer, ExternalClient, Mobile, Web, Signal.

EnExpirationFlags.description: Flags: names of the set bits joined by ", " ("GtC, Day"), "None" when none is set; a set bit without a name is "Bit<n>" (bit number). Bits: GtC = 0x1, Day = 0x2, Specified = 0x4, SpecifiedDay = 0x8. Accepted on input, never written: All = GtC, Day, Specified, SpecifiedDay.

EnFillingFlags.description: Flags: names of the set bits joined by ", " ("FoK, IoC"), "None" when none is set; a set bit without a name is "Bit<n>" (bit number). Bits: FoK = 0x1, IoC = 0x2, BoC = 0x4. Accepted on input, never written: All = FoK, IoC, BoC.

EnInstantFlags.description: Flags: names of the set bits joined by ", " ("FastConfirmation"), "None" when none is set; a set bit without a name is "Bit<n>" (bit number). Bits: FastConfirmation = 0x1.

EnInstantMode.description:
This enumeration is used in the following methods:
IMTConSymbol::IECheckMode IMTConGroupSymbol::IECheckMode
IMTConGroupSymbol::IECheckModeDefault

EnMarginCalcFlags.description: Flags: names of the set bits joined by ", " ("ClearAcc"), "None" when none is set; a set bit without a name is "Bit<n>" (bit number). Bits: ClearAcc = 0x1.

EnMarginFlags.description: Flags: names of the set bits joined by ", " ("CheckProcess, CheckSLTP"), "None" when none is set; a set bit without a name is "Bit<n>" (bit number). Bits: CheckProcess = 0x1, CheckSLTP = 0x2, HedgeLargeLeg = 0x4, ExcludePl = 0x8, RecalcRates = 0x10. Accepted on input, never written: All = CheckProcess, CheckSLTP, HedgeLargeLeg, ExcludePl.

EnOrderFlags.description: Flags: names of the set bits joined by ", " ("Market, Limit"), "None" when none is set; a set bit without a name is "Bit<n>" (bit number). Bits: Market = 0x1, Limit = 0x2, Stop = 0x4, StopLimit = 0x8, SL = 0x10, TP = 0x20, CloseBy = 0x40. Accepted on input, never written: All = Market, Limit, Stop, StopLimit, SL, TP, CloseBy.

EnPermissionsFlags.description: Flags: names of the set bits joined by ", " ("CertConfirm, EnableConnection"), "None" when none is set; a set bit without a name is "Bit<n>" (bit number). Bits: CertConfirm = 0x1, EnableConnection = 0x2, ResetPassword = 0x4, ForcedOtpUsage = 0x8, RiskWarning = 0x10, RegulationProtect = 0x20, NotifyDeals = 0x40, NotifyOrders = 0x80, NotifyBalances = 0x100. Accepted on input, never written: NotifyAll = NotifyDeals, NotifyOrders, NotifyBalances; All = CertConfirm, EnableConnection, ResetPassword, ForcedOtpUsage, RiskWarning, RegulationProtect, NotifyDeals, NotifyOrders, NotifyBalances.

EnReportsFlags.description: Flags: names of the set bits joined by ", " ("Email, Support"), "None" when none is set; a set bit without a name is "Bit<n>" (bit number). Bits: Email = 0x1, Support = 0x2, Statements = 0x4. Accepted on input, never written: All = Email, Statements.

EnRequestFlags.description: Flags: names of the set bits joined by ", " ("Order"), "None" when none is set; a set bit without a name is "Bit<n>" (bit number). Bits: Order = 0x1.

EnSwapFlags.description: Flags: names of the set bits joined by ", " ("ConsiderHolidays"), "None" when none is set; a set bit without a name is "Bit<n>" (bit number). Bits: ConsiderHolidays = 0x1.

EnTickFlags.description: Flags: names of the set bits joined by ", " ("Realtime, CollectRaw"), "None" when none is set; a set bit without a name is "Bit<n>" (bit number). Bits: Realtime = 0x1, CollectRaw = 0x2, FeedStats = 0x4, NegativePrices = 0x8. Accepted on input, never written: All = Realtime, CollectRaw, FeedStats, NegativePrices.

EnTradeFlags.description:
Common Trade Flags
Flags: names of the set bits joined by ", " ("ProfitByMarket, AllowSignals"), "None" when none is set; a set bit without a name is "Bit" (bit number). Bits: ProfitByMarket = 0x1, AllowSignals = 0x2. Accepted on input, never written: TradeFlagsAll = ProfitByMarket, AllowSignals.

EnTradeRightsFlags.description: Flags: names of the set bits joined by ", " ("Swaps, Trailing"), "None" when none is set; a set bit without a name is "Bit<n>" (bit number). Bits: Swaps = 0x1, Trailing = 0x2, Experts = 0x4, Expiration = 0x8, SignalsAll = 0x10, SignalsOwn = 0x20, SOCompensation = 0x40, SOFullyHedged = 0x80, FifoClose = 0x100, HedgeProhibit = 0x200, DealCost = 0x400, SOCompensationCredit = 0x800. Accepted on input, never written: Default = Swaps, Trailing, Experts, Expiration, SignalsAll; All = Swaps, Trailing, Experts, Expiration, SignalsAll, SignalsOwn, SOCompensation, SOFullyHedged, FifoClose, HedgeProhibit, DealCost, SOCompensationCredit.

GroupRights.description: Flags: names of the set bits joined by ", " ("Signals, Trailing"), "None" when none is set; a set bit without a name is "Bit<n>" (bit number). Bits: Signals = 0x1, Trailing = 0x2, Advisor = 0x4, Expiration = 0x8, SignalAll = 0x10, SignalsOwn = 0x20, RiskWarning = 0x40, ForcedOTPUsage = 0x80.

MT4BalanceDiff.description:
v2 DTO returned by `AdmBalanceCheck`. Reports the difference between
the account's recorded balance and what the MT4 server recomputes from
closed orders + balance operations. `Diff = 0` means the integrity
check passed; non-zero means the recorded balance has drifted and would
be set to `recorded + Diff` if `AdmBalanceFix` ran.

MT4DailyReport.description:
v2 DTO mirroring the platform's `DailyReport`: one end-of-day
balance/equity/PnL snapshot for a single account. Used by the broker
daily-report family (per-login query, bulk pull, incremental sync).
Internal underscore-prefixed unix-time field, the `Next` pointer
chain, and the 3-int `Reserved` padding are intentionally excluded.
Note: `Ctm` is reported by the MT4 server in its local time zone,
not UTC — clients should treat it as "broker day boundary" and convert
as appropriate.

balance.description: Balance at the end of the reporting day

balancePrev.description: Balance at the start of the reporting day

bank.description: Free-form bank/payment identifier recorded with the day's deposits

ctm.description: Day boundary timestamp (platform internal: __time32_t, server-local time)

deposit.description: Net deposits credited within the day (positive = inflow)

group.description: Trading group the account was in on that day

login.description: Account login the report belongs to

profitClosed.description: Closed-position profit/loss realised within the day

MT4Group.description:
v2 DTO describing a trading group configuration. Curated subset of the
the platform's `ConGroup` — exposes the configuration fields that callers
need to inspect margin/leverage/rights settings.
            
Deliberately omitted from v2 (vs v1's full ConGroup shape):
  * `SmtpServer`, `SmtpLogin`, `SmtpPassword` — SMTP
    credentials must never cross the v2 boundary regardless of access
    level. `SmtpServer` alone is dropped too because a server name
    is rarely useful without its credentials and exposes infra topology.
  * `Templates` — server-side filesystem path, irrelevant to API
    consumers and a minor information-disclosure risk.
  * `SecuritiesHash` — opaque byte[], platform bookkeeping.
  * `Reserved`, `UnusedRights`, `SecGroups[32]`,
    `SecMargins[128]` — reserved/internal arrays. The two nested
    arrays (SecGroups, SecMargins) deserve their own dedicated v2
    endpoints (`GroupSecGroupsGet/{group}`, `GroupSecMarginsGet/{group}`)
    planned for Wave 3 — including them here would balloon the DTO.
  * `NewsLanguages` (uint[]) and `NewsLanguagesTotal` —
    rarely consumed; can be added later once the use case is clear.
            
Enums (`OTPMode`, `MarginMode`, `NewsMode`,
`MarginControllingType`) are returned as their names;
`GroupRights` is a flags string, the names of the set bits.

archiveMaxBalance.description: Maximum balance under which an account is eligible for archiving

archivePeriod.description: Inactivity period (days) before account moves to archive

checkIEPrices.description: 0 = no IE check, non-zero = check Instant Execution prices

copies.description: Number of statement copies sent to support address

credit.description: Virtual credit applied to the group's accounts

defaultDeposit.description: Default deposit applied when an account omits its own balance

defaultLeverage.description: Default leverage applied when an account omits its own leverage

enable.description: 0 = group disabled, non-zero = enabled (accounts in this group can log in)

group.description: Group name (unique per platform, max 16 chars)

groupRights.description: Permissions bit mask for this group

hedgeLargeLeg.description: 0 = standard hedge, non-zero = treat large hedged leg specially

marginControllingType.description: Margin controlling unit (percent vs deposit currency)

marginMode.description: Margin calculation mode (don't use / use all / use profit / use loss)

maxPositions.description: Maximum simultaneous orders and open positions

reports.description: 0 = statements disabled, non-zero = nightly statements enabled

secMarginsTotal.description: Count of special securities settings (SecMargins) in use

stopoutSkipHedged.description: 0 = include hedged accounts in stop-out checks, non-zero = skip them

supportPage.description: Support page URL shown to clients

useSwap.description: 0 = no rollovers, non-zero = use rollovers and interest rate

pumping cache. Curated subset of the platform's NewsTopic: enough to render
a list / browse view of broker-distributed news (Key for follow-up

category.description:

keywords.description:

brokers as a symbol filter — for example `"!EURUSD, EUR*"`
selects all EUR pairs except EURUSD.

langId.description:

16 bits of a Windows LCID (the language portion).

time.description: Published time of the news topic (UTC).

topic.description: News headline / subject (max 256 chars at the platform layer).

MT4ServerTime.description:
v2 DTO for the MT4 server's per-hour access matrix (the platform's `ConTime.Days` field). 168-element flat array; each element is `0` (denied) or `1` (allowed) for one hour of the week. Layout: `index = day * 24 + hour`, day-of-week 0..6 matches MT4's native convention where day 0 = Sunday.

accessHours.description:
7×24 = 168 hourly access flags. Index = day*24 + hour;
day 0 = Sunday (MT4 convention). 0 = denied, 1 = allowed.

MT4SymbolConfigUpdate.description:
Type 1 mutator input for `CfgUpdateSymbol`. Same field set as the read
DTO MT4SymbolConfig minus:
  * `Symbol` (path parameter, immutable identity);
  * `Count`, `CountOriginal`, `FilterCounter` — server-side
    counters, derived;
  * Enum fields are submitted as their names.
            
Fields preserved by the server-side read step (NOT on this DTO):
  * `Symbol` identity.
  * `Sessions` nested array (own endpoint planned).
  * `Unused`, `ExternalUnused`, `ProfitReserved`,
    `FilterReserved` reserved arrays.
  * `Count`, `CountOriginal`, `FilterCounter`,
    `BidTickValue`, `AskTickValue`, `Point`, `Multiply`
    — server-derived from other fields, writing them is a no-op or
    overwrite-with-stale.

MT4SymbolInfo.description:
v2 DTO describing a single symbol's market data and metadata as held in
the platform's pumping cache. Curated subset of the platform's SymbolInfo:
covers what clients monitoring tick feeds / building a quote panel
actually need — current Bid/Ask, session High/Low, tick precision
(Digits, Point), current Spread (in points), last-tick direction, and

            observed a tick for this symbol since connect.

point.description: Point size (e.g. 0.00001 for 5-digit FX); price increment per point

type.description: Security group index this symbol belongs to (refers to ConGroupSec)

MT4TradeTransaction.description:
v2 DTO for a trade transaction — input AND output of `TradeTransaction`.
The platform's `TradeTransInfo` is in/out: the caller fills the request
fields (operation type, command, symbol, volume, price), submits via POST,
and the server populates the resulting `Order` id (for Open) or
echoes the modified record (for Modify/Close).
            
Enum fields (`TradeTransactionType`, `TradeCommand`,
`TradeRequestFlags`) are plain strings. Clients submit the name
(e.g. `"Buy"`, `"PendingOpen"`); the response echoes the names
back. Each field lists its valid names.

crc.description: CRC for transaction integrity; usually 0 (server fills).

expiration.description: Pending order expiration time. Default value means GTC.

order.description: Order ticket. 0 on Open requests; server fills this on success.

orderBy.description: Login (account number). Required for Balance/Credit operations.

tradeCommand.description:
Trade command. Empty means `Buy`.
One of: Buy, Sell, BuyLimit, SellLimit, BuyStop, SellStop, Balance, Credit. Case-insensitive; the numeric value is accepted too. Any other value is refused with error code Validation.

tradeRequestFlags.description:
Request flags (who placed the request). Empty means `None`.
Flags, names joined by ", ": None, Signal, Expert, Gateway, Mobile, Web, API. Case-insensitive; numbers are accepted.

tradeTransactionType.description:
Transaction type (required). Manager-side operations use the `Br*` types, e.g. `BrBalance` with trade command `Balance` or `Credit` for a balance or credit operation.
One of: PricesGet, PricesRequote, OpenInstant, OpenRequest, OpenMarket, PendingOpen, CloseInstant, CloseRequest, CloseMarket, Modify, Delete, CloseBy, CloseAll, BrOpen, BrClose, BrDelete, BrCloseBy, BrCloseAll, BrModify, BrActivate, BrComment, BrBalance. Case-insensitive; the numeric value is accepted too. Any other value is refused with error code Validation.

volume.description: Volume in MT4 internal units. 1 lot = 100, so e.g. 250 = 2.5 lots.

MT4TradeUpdate.description:
Type 1 mutator input for the admin direct-edit endpoint `AdmTradeRecordModify`. Only the fields a back-office tool would legitimately need to adjust are exposed; everything else (order id, login, symbol, volume, open/close times, gateway internals, conversion rates, API data blobs) is preserved from the server-side read.
For typical stop-loss / take-profit edits prefer `POST TradeTransaction` with `tradeTransactionType=BrModify` — that goes through the platform's audited path. This endpoint is the low-level admin override for back-office corrections.

order.description: Order ticket to edit (path parameter is the source of truth)

MT4User.description:
v2 DTO describing a trading account. Curated subset of the platform's
`UserRecord` — exposes identity, contact, financial and flag fields
that callers actually need.
            
Deliberately omitted from v2 (vs v1's full UserRecord shape):
  * Password / PasswordInvestor / PasswordPhone / OtpSecret / ApiData /
    SecureReserved — credentials and secrets must never cross the v2
    boundary regardless of access level.
  * Unused / Reserved2 / EnableReserved / TimeStamp — platform bookkeeping
    with no caller-visible semantics.
            
Account flags are exposed as a single MT4User.EnableFlags bitfield
(the platform's native representation). Bit semantics are documented under
that property — splitting it into separate booleans would hide the fact
that MetaQuotes occasionally reuses bit positions across builds.

agentAccount.description: IB / agent account number that referred this client

country.description: Country (free text per broker's enrolment workflow)

enableFlags.description:
Account flag bitfield (the platform's `EnableFlags`). Documented bits:
  * 0x01 = account enabled (login allowed)
  * 0x02 = client may change password
  * 0x04 = account is read-only (no trading)
  * 0x08 = OTP enrolment required at login
Bit positions reflect MT4 build 1455. Verify against the current MT4
Manager docs if pinning behaviour to a specific bit.

externalId.description: External customer identifier (e.g. CRM/KYC link). The platform's `Id` field.

group.description: Group name the account belongs to

interestRate.description: Interest rate (broker-defined, often used for swaps)

lastDate.description: UTC timestamp of the last MT4 server interaction

lastIP.description: Last connection IP as raw int (use platform helpers to format)

login.description: Trading account number (login)

mqid.description:
MetaQuotes ID for mobile push notifications (0 if not linked).
Typed as `long` in v2 even though current builds store it in
32 bits — the platform exposes a wider underlying type and a checked
narrowing cast would crash for accounts whose mqid sits above
Int32.MaxValue. Future-proofs the contract against MQ widening.

name.description: Display name of the account holder

prevBalance.description: Balance at the previous reporting close

prevEquity.description: Equity at the previous reporting close

prevMonthBalance.description: Balance at the start of the previous calendar month

prevMonthEquity.description: Equity at the start of the previous calendar month

registrationDate.description: UTC timestamp when the account was created

sendReports.description: 0 = no reports, non-zero = nightly email reports enabled

taxes.description: Tax rate applied to the account

userColor.description: UI tint color in terminal client lists

MT4UserCreate.description:
Type 1 mutator input — full create shape for `UserRecordNew`.
Same writable fields as MT4UserUpdate minus the explicit
`Balance`/`Credit` (those should come through dedicated balance
operations after the account exists). The platform allocates the next free
login id when `Login = 0`; clients may also request a specific id by
setting `Login > 0` (the server rejects collisions).
            
Password / OTP / API-data fields are NOT on this DTO. After successful
creation, set the initial password via a separate
`POST UserPasswordSet/{login}` call. The platform accepts the new
account with empty password bytes; the password endpoint lifts it to
usable credentials.

login.description:
Optional preferred login. `0` = let server assign the next free
id. `> 0` = request this exact id (server rejects collisions
via platform error code).

MT5ChartBarV2.description:
One OHLC bar of a symbol's chart history, v2 read DTO. The trade server keeps
history as minutes; bars of a coarser period are aggregated from those minutes
on the boundaries of the server's trading time.

close.description: Close price — the price at the end of the bar's minute.

dateTime.description: The same bar opening time as a date-time without offset, for direct display.

high.description: Highest price reached inside the bar.

low.description: Lowest price reached inside the bar.

open.description: Open price — the price at the beginning of the bar's minute.

spread.description: Lowest spread, in points, recorded while the bar was forming.

tickVolume.description:
Tick volume: the number of incoming ticks that moved the quote during the bar.
Consecutive ticks with the same price count once.

time.description: Bar opening time — seconds since 01.01.1970, in the trade server's trading time.

volume.description: Real traded volume executed during the bar.

MT5ChartPeriod.description:
Bar period of a chart history request. Coarser bars than a minute are built by the
service from the minute history of the trade server, on the boundaries of the trade
server's trading time — a day therefore starts at 00:00 of the server clock.

MT5ChartRoundingRule.description: Rounding rule applied to prices converted by a split.

companyRegDate.description: Company registration date in seconds that elapsed since 01.01.1970 (UnixTime).

personBirthDate.description:
person birth date
The date of birth is specified in the FILETIME format: the number of 100-nanosecond intervals that have elapsed since January 1, 1601

personDocumentDate.description:
issue date of the identification document (of passport, driver's license, etc.).
in seconds since 01.01.1970 (UnixTime).

agentMonthly.description: Agent commission charged for the trade operations of the current month.

balance.description: Balance of the account at the report time.

balancePrevDay.description: Balance of the account at the end of the previous day.

balancePrevMonth.description: Balance of the account at the end of the previous month.

commissionMonthly.description: Commissions charged from the account during the current month.

credit.description: Amount of credit funds of the account at the report time.

currencyDigits.description: Number of decimal places of the deposit currency.

dailyAgent.description: Agent commission charged for the trade operations of the reported day.

dailyCommFee.description: Fee charged for the deals of the account during the reported day.

dailyCommRound.description: Turnover commissions charged from the account during the reported day.

dailyCorrection.description: Corrective balance operations of the reported day.

dailyCredit.description: Credit given to the account during the reported day.

dailyDividend.description: Dividends accrued to the account for the reported day.

dailyInterest.description: Amount accrued to the account under the annual interest rate for the reported day.

dailyProfit.description: Profit of the account for the reported day.

dailySOCompensation.description: Negative balance compensation accrued to the account for the reported day.

dailySOCompensationCredit.description: Credit funds withdrawn during the reported day as a result of a negative balance compensation.

dailyStorage.description: Swaps calculated for the account for the reported day.

dailyTaxes.description: Taxes withheld from the funds of the account for the reported day.

datetime.description: Time the report was generated, in seconds since 01.01.1970 as the trade server counts them.

datetimePrev.description: Time of the previous report of the same account, in seconds since 01.01.1970.

equityPrevDay.description: Equity of the account at the end of the previous day.

equityPrevMonth.description: Equity of the account at the end of the previous month.

group.description: Group of the account.

interestRate.description: Annual interest rate of the account, in percent.

login.description: Login of the account the report belongs to.

margin.description: Margin reserved for the open positions of the account.

marginLevel.description: Margin level of the account, in percent.

name.description: Name of the account holder as stored in the account.

orders.description: Pending orders of the account; `null` in a lightweight report.

positions.description: Open positions of the account; `null` in a lightweight report.

profit.description: Current profit of all open positions of the account.

profitEquity.description: Current floating equity of the account.

profitStorage.description: Swaps charged for the open positions of the account but not yet reflected in the balance.

MT5UserRights.description:
MT5 user permission flags. Values mirror CIMTUser.EnUsersRights.
Flags: names of the set bits joined by ", " ("Enabled, Password"), "None" when none is set; a set bit without a name is "Bit" (bit number). info.description:
Works with MetaTrader 4 and MetaTrader 5 trade servers and keeps a live connection to each of them, so the `…Get` calls answer from it much faster than the `…Request` calls, which ask the trade server every time.

Partly follows the JSON-Pure API idea: a successful call answers HTTP 200; any other code reports an error, such as wrong parameters or an unavailable trade platform.
info.title: JSON-Pure WebAPI for MT4/MT5

get.description:
Admin balance integrity check for a batch of accounts.
            
Same semantics as the single-login variant but takes a list of logins
via repeated query parameters: `?logins=1001&logins=1002`.
One billed Manager request regardless of the array length. The response
list contains entries only for accounts the server flagged with a
non-zero diff — clean accounts are silently omitted. Clients should
treat "missing from response" as "diff = 0".

**Timeout:** 10 s by default, adjustable per request with the `X-Request-Timeout` header. When the trade server does not answer in time: Nothing was changed; the request is safe to repeat.

parameters.description: Trade platform id (GUID)
parameters.name: tradePlatform

parameters.description: Account logins (repeat query parameter)
parameters.name: logins

parameters.description: How long to wait for the trade server, in seconds (1–300). Default for this operation: 10 s (read). The query parameter `requestTimeout` does the same for clients that cannot set headers. The applied value is returned in the `X-Request-Timeout-Applied` response header.
parameters.name: X-Request-Timeout

get.description:
Admin balance integrity check for a single account.
            
Manager (live) call. Returns the difference between the recorded
account balance and what the MT4 server recomputes from closed
orders + balance operations. `diff = 0` → balance is intact;
non-zero → admin tooling can run `AdmBalanceFix` to recompute
(forthcoming Wave 3 endpoint).
            
Read-only operation despite the platform's "Adm" prefix (the prefix
signals the elevated authorization requirement, not a write side
effect).

**Timeout:** 10 s by default, adjustable per request with the `X-Request-Timeout` header. When the trade server does not answer in time: Nothing was changed; the request is safe to repeat.

parameters.description: Trade platform id (GUID)
parameters.name: tradePlatform

parameters.description: Account login (positive integer)
parameters.name: login

parameters.description: How long to wait for the trade server, in seconds (1–300). Default for this operation: 10 s (read). The query parameter `requestTimeout` does the same for clients that cannot set headers. The applied value is returned in the `X-Request-Timeout-Applied` response header.
parameters.name: X-Request-Timeout

post.description:
Admin balance fix — recompute balances for the given logins.
            
POST mutator. Asks MT4 server to take the diffs reported by
`AdmBalanceCheck` and write them onto the accounts. Empty body —
the logins are submitted as repeated query parameters
(`?logins=1001&logins=1002`) to keep the URL shape parallel
with the read variant and avoid the awkward "POST with int[] body"
pattern.
            
This DOES modify account balances. Pair every retry with an
`Idempotency-Key` header; otherwise a retried fix can double-
apply on an account whose original fix happened to land but whose
response was lost on the wire.

**Timeout:** 5 s by default, adjustable per request with the `X-Request-Timeout` header. When the trade server does not answer in time: The operation may still be completed by the server (`X-Request-Outcome: unknown`): check its result before repeating it.

parameters.description: Trade platform id (GUID)
parameters.name: tradePlatform

parameters.description: Account logins to fix (repeat query parameter)
parameters.name: logins

parameters.description: How long to wait for the trade server, in seconds (1–300). Default for this operation: 5 s (trade operation). The query parameter `requestTimeout` does the same for clients that cannot set headers. The applied value is returned in the `X-Request-Timeout-Applied` response header.
parameters.name: X-Request-Timeout

post.description:
Admin direct edit of a single trade record — Type 1 with read-first.
Low-level back-office override that writes directly to the trade record. For SL/TP edits prefer `POST TradeTransaction` with `tradeTransactionType=BrModify` — that route goes through the platform's audited path. Use this endpoint for manual accounting corrections (commission/storage/taxes/ profit, comment, magic) that the standard TradeTransaction path does not cover.
Flow: read existing trade via `TradeRecordsRequest`, patch the allow-listed fields in place, submit via `AdmTradeRecordModify`. Order/Login/Symbol/Volume/OpenPrice/OpenTime/CloseTime and gateway internals are preserved by virtue of not being on the input DTO.
Idempotency-Key strongly recommended. A retried edit without it can land twice — usually harmless, but generates audit log noise. **Timeout:** 5 s by default, adjustable per request with the `X-Request-Timeout` header. When the trade server does not answer in time: The operation may still be completed by the server (`X-Request-Outcome: unknown`): check its result before repeating it.

parameters.name: tradePlatform

parameters.description: Order ticket (path)
parameters.name: ticket

The query parameter `requestTimeout` does the same for clients that cannot set headers. The applied value is returned in the `X-Request-Timeout-Applied` response header.
parameters.name: X-Request-Timeout

post.description:
Bulk-deletes a list of trade tickets (administrative scope). Used for cleanup after reconciliation mistakes, simulator state reset, or compliance-mandated removal.
            
Manager-live POST. The platform accepts a flat `int[]` of order
tickets and a count; we mirror the existing batched-int pattern
(repeat `?orders=` per ticket — same convention as
`UserRecordsRequest`'s `?logins=`). Empty arrays are
rejected with Validation.
            
**Destructive.** Each ticket in the array is removed from the
server's trade table; this is not reversible from the API side.
Pair with `Idempotency-Key` so retries don't re-process partial
failures.

**Timeout:** 5 s by default, adjustable per request with the `X-Request-Timeout` header. When the trade server does not answer in time: The operation may still be completed by the server (`X-Request-Outcome: unknown`): check its result before repeating it.

parameters.description: Trade platform id (GUID)
parameters.name: tradePlatform

parameters.description:
Order tickets to delete (repeat the query
             parameter — must be non-empty)
parameters.name: orders

parameters.description: How long to wait for the trade server, in seconds (1–300). Default for this operation: 5 s (trade operation). The query parameter `requestTimeout` does the same for clients that cannot set headers. The applied value is returned in the `X-Request-Timeout-Applied` response header.
parameters.name: X-Request-Timeout

get.description:
All trades belonging to accounts in a given group (admin scope).
            
Manager (live) call. Returns trades for every account assigned to
the given group. `openOnly=true` filters out closed trades on
the server side. Pair with `Idempotency-Key` on retry — large
groups can return substantial payloads.

**Timeout:** 30 s by default, adjustable per request with the `X-Request-Timeout` header. When the trade server does not answer in time: Nothing was changed; the request is safe to repeat.

The query parameter `requestTimeout` does the same for clients that cannot set headers. The applied value is returned in the `X-Request-Timeout-Applied` response header.

get.description:
All user accounts in a given group (admin scope) — the safe variant that honors permission checks server-side.
            
Manager (live) call. Returns the curated `MT4User` projection
for every account in the specified group. The platform's "Safe" suffix
indicates it runs through `RunSafe` with the `Admin` rights
guard — a manager lacking that permission receives a sensible error
rather than a connection drop.
            
Comma-separated group lists are accepted by the platform (it strips
commas and trims whitespace internally); the simplest call pattern
is a single group name. Large groups may return substantial
payloads — pair with `Idempotency-Key` on retry.

**Timeout:** 30 s by default, adjustable per request with the `X-Request-Timeout` header. When the trade server does not answer in time: Nothing was changed; the request is safe to repeat.

`BackupRequestOrders(string file, string request)`. Order-side
counterpart of `BackupRequestUsers`. Same caveats:
read-only, full file loaded server-side regardless of `limit`,

get.description:
Read user records out of a backup file (does NOT restore — read-only). Manager (live) call to the platform's `BackupRequestUsers(string file, string request)`. The platform extracts records from the named backup file but does NOT write them back to the live DB — that requires a separate (destructive) `BackupRestoreUsers` call which is part of Wave 4b.
Use `BackupInfoUsers` first to discover valid file names. The optional `request` query is a server-defined filter string; empty string returns all users.
Heavy operation: backup files can contain millions of records — the platform returns the full set in one shot. The optional `limit` query truncates the response server-side (default 10000, max 100000). The platform still loads the full file regardless of limit — limit only caps the JSON response size. **Timeout:** 30 s by default, adjustable per request with the `X-Request-Timeout` header. When the trade server does not answer in time: Nothing was changed; the request is safe to repeat.

post.description:
Restore order records into the live MT4 database. Destructive — requires `?confirm=true`. Manager (live) call to the platform's `BackupRestoreOrders(TradeRecord[] trades)`. Returns `MT4TradeRestoreResult[]` — one entry per input trade, with `Order` (ticket) and `Res` (0 = error, 1 = restored). Position in the response array matches position in the request.
Idempotency-Key header is strongly recommended. Batch cap: 10000 records per call. **Timeout:** 60 s by default, adjustable per request with the `X-Request-Timeout` header. When the trade server does not answer in time: The operation may still be completed by the server (`X-Request-Outcome: unknown`): check its result before repeating it.

parameters.name: tradePlatform

parameters.description: Required deliberateness flag — must equal `true`
parameters.name: confirm

parameters.description: How long to wait for the trade server, in seconds (1–300). Default for this operation: 60 s (server maintenance). The query parameter `requestTimeout` does the same for clients that cannot set headers. The applied value is returned in the `X-Request-Timeout-Applied` response header.
parameters.name: X-Request-Timeout

requestBody.description: Array of trades to restore (1..10000 records)

post.description:
Restore user records into the live MT4 database. Destructive — requires `?confirm=true`. Manager (live) call to the platform's `BackupRestoreUsers(UserRecord[] users)`. Each input `MT4UserRestoreInput` is mapped to a fresh `UserRecord` with the narrow restore field set — secrets, OTP, server-managed timestamps, and reserved blobs are NOT carried (see DTO docs).
Idempotency-Key header is strongly recommended: a network blip during a multi-user restore can leave the client uncertain whether the write happened. Without the key, retry will double-write.
Batch cap: 10000 records per call. Larger restores must be split. **Timeout:** 60 s by default, adjustable per request with the `X-Request-Timeout` header. Change server-wide common settings. Only the fields present in the body are written: the
current record is read from the trade server, the body is applied over it, and the merged
record is written back. A field that is left out keeps its server value; for the string
fields, omitting the key keeps the value while sending `""` clears it. A body without
any field is rejected.
            
Preserved fields the DTO does not touch:
<list type="bullet"><item>Runtime counters (LastOrder, LastLogin, LostLogin,
        optimization timestamps, overnight rollover state).</item><item>Protocol identity (ServerVersion, ServerBuild).</item><item>Bind / web address arrays (variable-length nested
        collections — own endpoints planned).</item><item>Demo-account subsystem, paths, rollover/statement modes
        (sensitive admin areas with separate endpoints).</item></list>
            
Idempotency-Key strongly recommended — overwriting common settings
affects every connected client.

Update the 7×24 access-hour matrix — Type 1 mutator.
            
Manager (live) call. Reads the current `ConTime`, replaces the
168-hour access matrix with the supplied `AccessHours`, and
writes back. The platform's internal `DaysControl` (server
housekeeping) and `Reserved` (forward-compat padding) fields
are preserved across the round-trip.
            
`AccessHours` must be exactly 168 entries long; index =
`day * 24 + hour` with day 0 = Sunday. Each value is
`0` (denied) or `1` (allowed) — any other value is
passed through verbatim (the platform does not validate, and
MT4 may treat anything non-zero as allowed depending on build).
            
Echoes the merged `MT4ServerTime` in the response.

**Timeout:** 15 s by default, adjustable per request with the `X-Request-Timeout` header. When the trade server does not answer in time: The operation may still be completed by the server (`X-Request-Outcome: unknown`): check its result before repeating it.

get.description:
End-of-day balance/equity/PnL snapshots for a batch of account logins within a date window — the broker daily-report data set, flat shape (one row per (login, day) pair).
            
Manager-live read (round-trip to MT4 server). Pass logins as repeated
query parameters: `?logins=1001&logins=1002&logins=1003`.
Server-side billing counts this as one Manager request regardless of
batch size — prefer one batched call over a per-login loop.
            
Each row carries its own `Login` field, so the flat shape is
joinable on the client side. The MT4 server returns dates in its
local time zone, **not** UTC — clients should treat `Ctm` as
"broker day boundary" and convert as appropriate.
            
Note: the platform warns that asking for a window where the manager
account lacks the `Automatic server reports` permission may
cause MT4 to drop the manager connection. The API-side
`ResourceAccess` check is an indirect guard; a broker that
mis-configured the underlying manager rights can still observe
transient connection bounces.

**Timeout:** 30 s by default, adjustable per request with the `X-Request-Timeout` header. When the trade server does not answer in time: Nothing was changed; the request is safe to repeat.

post.description:
Opens a server-side incremental sync session for daily reports modified at or after timestamp. Follow up with `DailySyncRead` to retrieve the snapshot.
            
Manager-live POST (modifies server-side session state). The two-call
cycle `DailySyncStart → DailySyncRead` is the broker pattern for
pulling only-changed-since-last-poll daily reports; pass
`timestamp=0` to request all records.
            
`timestamp` is a Unix epoch second (int32) in MT4 server-local
time, not UTC. Platform marshals it directly to `__time32_t` —
pre-1970 / post-2038 values are out of range.
            
Returns a bare success envelope (no payload); the actual data comes
from a subsequent `DailySyncRead` call.

post.description:
Pass arbitrary binary payload to the MT4 server's plugin pipeline.
Manager (live) call via the platform's `ExternalCommandCustom` overload with a pass-through byte-array marshaller. The first installed plugin that returns `RET_OK` wins; its response bytes become the payload's `Data` field.
Wire format: `byte[]` serializes as base64 in JSON. Clients agree with the plugin author on the binary layout.
Why sidecar-only: the platform's binary variants rely on `Marshal.SizeOf` + native `ExternalCommand` dispatch. On `mtmanapi64.dll` the signed/unsigned marshalling diverges from `mtmanapi.dll` — same payload byte-for-byte can decode differently on x64. The x86 sidecar process loads the 32-bit DLL where the marshalling is the original one.
The platform's third `ExternalCommandCustom` overload that takes an `ICustomSerializer` interface is genuinely not REST-translatable — it requires the caller to provide C# serialization logic in-process. Not exposed. **Timeout:** 60 s by default, adjustable per request with the `X-Request-Timeout` header. When the trade server does not answer in time: The operation may still be completed by the server (`X-Request-Outcome: unknown`): check its result before repeating it.

post.description:
Plugin custom-command channel with JSON payload in both directions.
            
Manager (live) call wrapping `ExternalCommandJSON`. The MT4
server forwards the body to whichever installed plugin claims the
command first; the first plugin returning `RET_OK` wins and its
response becomes the v2 payload. The request body is sent verbatim
(no field renaming, no schema enforcement) so the plugin author
owns the over-the-wire contract on both ends.
            
The platform trio (`ExternalCommand<TIn,TOut>` for binary
marshal, `ExternalCommandCustom<T>` for caller-supplied
serializer) is intentionally not exposed in v2 — those variants
require compile-time struct layouts shared between client and
plugin, which a REST surface cannot guarantee. Plugin developers
who need binary transport should keep using the platform directly
from the WebAPI process or build a dedicated binary endpoint.
            
Idempotency-Key is strongly recommended — plugins may have side
effects, and the channel itself gives no read-modify-write
semantics.

**Timeout:** 60 s by default, adjustable per request with the `X-Request-Timeout` header. When the trade server does not answer in time: The operation may still be completed by the server (`X-Request-Outcome: unknown`): check its result before repeating it.

Manager (live) call. The MT4 server walks the symbol's full bar
history for every period and fixes inconsistencies (gaps, broken

kick off a second full sweep.

get.description:
Closed-trade reports for a batch of account logins within a time window — the data set that drives broker financial reporting (PnL, commissions, taxes) and customer trade-history exports.
            
Manager-live read (round-trip to MT4 server). Pass logins as repeated
query parameters: `?logins=1001&logins=1002&logins=1003`.
Server-side billing counts this as one Manager request regardless of
batch size — prefer one batched call over a per-login loop.
            
The platform returns a dictionary keyed by order ticket; the v2 envelope
flattens it to a list. Missing logins are silently omitted (no error
envelope). The optional name parameter selects a
server-defined report template — leave it null/empty to use the
default `"RTL_report"` template (closed trades within the window).
            
Pump cache is NOT consulted — data reflects authoritative server
history. Note: the platform comment warns that asking for a window
where the manager account lacks the `Reports` permission may
cause MT4 to drop the manager connection; this endpoint guards that
indirectly via the API-side `ResourceAccess` check, but a broker
that mis-configured the underlying manager rights can still observe
transient connection bounces.

**Timeout:** 30 s by default, adjustable per request with the `X-Request-Timeout` header. When the trade server does not answer in time: Nothing was changed; the request is safe to repeat.

Submit a trade transaction — open / modify / close / balance op.
POST mutator covering every platform trade operation through the single `TradeTransaction` entry point. The request body's `tradeTransactionType` + `tradeCommand` combination selects the actual operation — `OpenMarket`+`Buy`, `PendingOpen`+`BuyLimit`, `CloseMarket`+`Sell`, and the manager-side `Br*` types: `BrModify` (open price, SL, TP of an order), `BrDelete`, `BrBalance`+`Balance` or `Credit` (balance/credit operation on `orderBy`). get.description:
OHLC bars of a symbol for a time window, ordered by time ascending. The trade server keeps history as minutes; bars of a coarser `period` are aggregated from those minutes on the boundaries of the server's trading time, so a day starts at 00:00 of the server clock. A bar opens with the first minute of the bucket and closes with the last one, its high and low are the extremes of the bucket, tick volume and real volume are summed, and spread is the lowest of the bucket. Buckets without minutes are not produced.
Times are the trading times of the trade server, not UTC: `time` repeats the seconds-from-1970 value the platform uses, `dateTime` is the same moment without an offset. Prices are returned as the platform holds them, without rescaling.
`from` and `to` are optional: without `from` the window starts at the beginning of the history, without `to` it ends at the current server time. `limit` is 0 by default and returns the whole window; a positive value caps the returned bars and sets `truncated`. There is no pagination: to read further, repeat the request with `from` moved past the last returned bar.
The call only reads and changes nothing. When the platform has not received the requested history yet, the call fails with the platform code `MT_RET_OK_NONE` and a message saying the history is not synchronized — such a request may be repeated later. `W1` and `MN1` are rejected: such bars are not built. **Timeout:** 30 s by default, adjustable per request with the `X-Request-Timeout` header. When the trade server does not answer in time: Nothing was changed; the request is safe to repeat.

day, together with the positions and pending orders that were open at the end of that day.

requires, which is what separates this call from storing a deal record. Login, symbol,
action, volume and price are mandatory; the closing of a position under the hedged

post.description:
Takes the request at the head of the queue and reserves it for this connection: the trade server will not hand it to another dealer and waits for the answer. The request must be answered with `DealerAnswer`; an unanswered request is not returned to the queue and is lost.
The call is a write, not a read for all practical purposes: it changes the state of the queue and cannot be safely repeated — a repeated call takes the next request. When the queue is empty the platform answers `MT_RET_OK_NONE`. The queue must be opened with `DealerStart` first. **Timeout:** 15 s by default, adjustable per request with the `X-Request-Timeout` header. When the trade server does not answer in time: The operation may still be completed by the server (`X-Request-Outcome: unknown`): check its result before repeating it.

post.description:
Subscribes the connection to the queue of trade requests of the trade server and loads the requests already waiting in it. From that moment the queue can be read and the requests can be taken for processing — by this connection only, and the subscription lives until the queue is closed or the connection is lost.
The call does not take a request and does not answer one: it only enables the queue. Repeating it on a connection whose queue is already open is harmless. **Timeout:** 15 s by default, adjustable per request with the `X-Request-Timeout` header. When the trade server does not answer in time: The operation may still be completed by the server (`X-Request-Outcome: unknown`): check its result before repeating it.

Stops dealing on the connection: the queue is no longer read or taken from, and the requests waiting in it stay in the queue for other dealers. Requests already taken for processing are not returned to the queue — they must still be answered.
The queue applies to the whole connection to the trade platform, so closing it affects every call that reads or takes requests from it. Repeating the call is harmless. **Timeout:** 15 s by default, adjustable per request with the `X-Request-Timeout` header. When the trade server does not answer in time: The operation may still be completed by the server (`X-Request-Outcome: unknown`): check its result before repeating it.

Only the fields the trading platform lets a manager change are accepted: the margin call level, the stop out level, the mode used to check them and the group trade options. A field left out of the body keeps its current value, and a body without any field is rejected.
The configuration is read from the trade server first, the body is applied over it and the result is written back, so a request never overwrites values it does not mention. post.description:
Makes the orders, positions and balance of the account match the passed state. The trade server compares the lists with its own data and performs the difference as deals with the `sync` reason: positions missing on one side are opened or closed, positions whose direction, price or contract size changed are reopened, a volume change is corrected, and a balance difference becomes a balance or correction deal. All of it stays in the trading history of the client.
The operation is heavy and changes money and positions: it must be used by the system that owns the account, not as a general-purpose edit. An omitted order or position list leaves that part untouched; an empty list states that the account has none and closes the existing ones. The call answers as soon as the trade server has accepted it, and the resulting state of the account is reported to the platform journal. **Timeout:** 5 s by default, adjustable per request with the `X-Request-Timeout` header. post.description:
Creates a trading account on the trade server. Every field of the record is optional: a field left out is not written to the new account, so it keeps the value the platform starts it with — and that value is `None` for rights, so an account created without `rights` cannot log in until the flag is granted. Send `rights` (at least `Enabled`) to make the account usable. A real trade server also refuses creation without a leverage (`MT_RET_ERR_PARAMS`): send `leverage` together with the group.
When the login field is absent or zero the server allocates one from the available range; when no logins are left the call fails with the platform error `MT_RET_USR_LOGIN_EXHAUSTED`. The group must be set, as well as the first or the last name of the account holder; otherwise the call fails with `MT_RET_ERR_PARAMS`. Adding an account whose login already exists fails with `MT_RET_USR_LOGIN_EXIST`.
Passwords are checked against the group policy. When either the master or the investor password is absent, both are regenerated to the group minimum length; a password the policy refuses is replaced with a fresh pair and the creation is repeated up to ten times. A failure of any other kind ends the call at once — a retry after a timeout could create a second account, since the first attempt may have succeeded unseen. The response carries the record as stored by the server, including the allocated login. **Timeout:** 15 s by default, adjustable per request with the `X-Request-Timeout` header. When the trade server does not answer in time: The operation may still be completed by the server (`X-Request-Outcome: unknown`): check its result before repeating it.

post.description:
Changes the account named by the `login` query parameter. Only the fields present in the body are written: the record is read from the trade server, the body is applied over it, and the merged record is written back. A field left out keeps its server value; for the string fields, omitting the key keeps the value while sending `""` clears it. A body without any field is rejected. The body must be the user update object — a full user record is not accepted.
The login identifies the record and is not part of the body; it is never changed by this call. An unknown login is answered with the trade server's error code. An unknown value of an enum field is answered as a validation error. The response is the updated record. **Timeout:** 15 s by default, adjustable per request with the `X-Request-Timeout` header. When the trade server does not answer in time: The operation may still be completed by the server (`X-Request-Outcome: unknown`): check its result before repeating it.
